data.q: What is the primary entry point for an Actix Web application?
data.e: Actix Web uses the #[actix_web::main] attribute (or #[actix_rt::main] in older versions) to mark the async main function that starts the server.

data.q: How do you define a route handler that responds to GET requests at path "/hello"?
o: Both A and B are valid
data.e: Both the route() method on App and the resource()/route() pattern are valid ways to define routes in Actix Web.

data.q: Which trait must a handler function return type implement to be used as a responder?
data.e: The Responder trait is implemented by types that can be converted into an HTTP response. Handler functions must return a type implementing Responder.

data.q: How do you extract path parameters from a request URL like "/users/{id}"?
data.e: Path<T> extracts path parameters into a tuple or struct. Query extracts query strings, Json extracts JSON bodies, and Data extracts shared application state.

data.q: What is the purpose of the `web::Data<T>` extractor?
o: To share application state across handlers
data.e: web::Data<T> provides shared, thread-safe access to application state (Arc<T>) across all handlers and middleware.

data.q: Which middleware is built-in for logging requests in Actix Web?
data.e: actix_web::middleware::Logger provides request logging. It is typically added via .wrap(middleware::Logger::default()).

data.q: How do you return a custom HTTP status code (e.g., 201 Created) with a JSON body?
data.e: All three approaches work: using the status-specific method (Created()), the generic status() builder, or the build() method with StatusCode enum.

data.q: What does the `#[derive(Deserialize)]` attribute enable when used with `web::Json<T>`?
o: Automatic parsing of JSON request bodies into struct T
data.e: web::Json<T> uses serde's Deserialize trait to automatically parse incoming JSON request bodies into the target type T.

data.q: How do you handle blocking operations (like DB calls) without blocking the Actix runtime?
o: Use async/await directly on blocking functions
data.e: web::block() (Actix helper) or tokio::task::spawn_blocking() offload blocking work to a separate thread pool, preventing executor starvation.

data.q: What is the correct way to serve static files from a directory "./static" at URL path "/static"?
data.e: actix_files::Files (or actix_web::web::Fs in older versions) serves static files. The first argument is the URL path prefix, the second is the filesystem path.

data.q: Which extractor is used to access HTTP headers in a handler?
data.e: You can use Header<T> to extract a specific header, HttpRequest to access the full request including headers(), or HeaderMap directly for all headers.

data.q: How do you configure a custom error response for a specific error type in Actix Web?
o: Implement ResponseError trait for your error type
data.e: ResponseError trait allows custom error -> response mapping. JsonConfig error_handler handles JSON parsing errors. ErrorHandlers middleware handles HTTP status error pages.

data.q: What is the role of the `Scope` in Actix Web routing?
o: To group routes under a common path prefix
To limit the scope of middleware
data.e: web::Scope groups routes under a path prefix (e.g., /api/v1) and can have its own middleware, guards, and default headers.

data.q: How do you test an Actix Web handler in isolation?
o: Use actix_web::test::TestRequest and call handler directly
Use actix_web::test::call_service with a test App
Use reqwest to hit a running test server
data.e: actix_web::test provides TestRequest for unit-testing handlers directly and call_service for integration-style testing with a full App.

data.q: Which feature flag enables TLS/HTTPS support in Actix Web's HttpServer?
data.e: Actix Web supports multiple TLS backends via feature flags: rustls-tls, native-tls, and openssl. You choose one at compile time.

data.q: What does the `guard` module provide in Actix Web routing?
o: Conditional route matching (e.g., by header, method, host)
data.e: actix_web::guard provides Guard types (Header, Query, Host, etc.) to conditionally match routes based on request properties beyond just path and method.
